context.problemStatement:
Implement the `Lambda` case of `eval`. An anonymous function `fn(x) { ... }`
evaluates to a function value. Nothing in its body is evaluated until it is
called, so this case never returns an error. Build a `VFunc(UserFn(...))` whose
name is `"lambda"` (used in error messages) and whose parent is the environment
in which this function was *defined*, not the one in which it will be called. This
is what lets a function use the names around it, even after the call that created it
has returned.

```
// In eval:
    Lambda(params, body) ->
      // YOUR CODE HERE (replace the code below)
      Error(errors.NotImplemented(
        "Lambda("
        <> string.inspect(params)
        <> ", "
        <> string.inspect(body)
        <> ")",
      ))
```

Run the tests:

```
gleam test -- q8
```

targets.claim: Student can explain why their Lambda case never returns an error even when the body of the anonymous function uses an unbound name, and when such an error would appear instead.

probes.question: In your `Lambda(params, body)` arm, why does evaluating `Lambda(["x"], Var("unbound"))` return `Ok` rather than an error, and when would that unbound variable actually cause an error?
probes.reason: Directly probes the student to explain why constructing a closure does not evaluate its body, and identifies function application as the point where body evaluation and potential errors happen.

probes.question: Your `Lambda` arm immediately wraps `UserFn("lambda", params, body, env)` in `Ok(VFunc(...))`. What part of `body` gets evaluated when this arm runs, and what specific action causes errors inside `body` to be detected?
probes.reason: Offers an alternative probe focusing on the AST expressions stored in `UserFn` to verify that execution of the body is deferred until the function is invoked.
